proposals.evidence: DEDR 561 documents Kannada ugur, Kodagu oy, Gondi gōr, Kurukh orox, Kuwi gōru with plural gōrka, Malto orgu and Toda ǖr as the nail/claw family. Survey final vowels and plural-looking material remain unchanged. Badaga ugilə is a comparative extension explicitly described as a look-alike in the source; Kodagu voyi and Toda yūr retain their initial glide/transcription differences. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3986(a) documents the pal tooth family: Kodagu pallï, Malayalam pallu, Tamil pal, Malto palu, Kolami pal, Gadaba pal/pallū with plural palkīl, and Toda pas̱. Survey plural and final-vowel material (including palku, pālkill, pāldu) remains unchanged. Toda parse is a comparative correspondence to its distinctive s̱ reflex; Betta Kurumba pallə extends the comparison to a lect absent from this article. Subsection (b) toothstick compounds are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 1931 gives Kurukh xẽs blood, xẽso red/blood and Malto qéso red. Source cognacy identifies this article. Survey Kurukh kʰēns/kheso retain their transcription of frication/nasality; Malto ēso is a comparative proposal whose missing initial q- remains visible for review, not silently repaired. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5517 explicitly gives Kannada beṅki fire, Malto béru sun, Brahui bāsing become hot and Ollari Gadaba veytal hot (in veytal nīr hot water). The source annotation identifies the family; survey benki, bērdu, bāsun and veṭal preserve their consonant and ending differences. The Gadaba survey response is the heat word alone, so no water component is inferred. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 1514 directly gives Kodagu tittï, Kolami kis, Malto cicu and Toda tït fire. Badaga kiccə is supported indirectly by the article’s explicit identification of Toda kic as a Badaga loan; this proposal is for the Badaga source form, not for the borrowed Toda song word. Survey titta, kiss, cicadu and tīttə preserve their endings and transcriptions. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
